hero.title: Coordinate Geometry — Bridging Algebra and Geometry
hero.hook: René Descartes was lying in bed watching a fly move on the ceiling when he had a flash of insight: you can describe any point's position using just two numbers. That idea — the coordinate system — transformed all of mathematics. And in Class 10, it gives you powerful tools to find distances, divide segments, and calculate areas using pure algebra.

hook_section.scenario: Two cities A(2,3) and B(8,7) are marked on a map. What's the straight-line distance between them? Without coordinate geometry, you'd need a ruler and scale drawing. With the distance formula: d = √[(8−2)² + (7−3)²] = √[36+16] = √52 ≈ 7.2 units. The same approach works for finding the midpoint, dividing a line in a ratio, or calculating the area of a triangle from its vertices.
hook_section.bridge: Chapter 7 covers four formulas: Distance Formula, Section Formula, Midpoint Formula, and Area of Triangle. These are tested almost every year in Class 10 boards, usually as 2–4 mark problems with specific coordinates given.
hook_section.punchline: Learn these four formulas cold: Distance Formula, Section Formula (m:n ratio), Midpoint Formula, Area of Triangle. Apply them mechanically — most marks are for correct substitution.

concept_section.analogy: Think of coordinate geometry as GPS for maths. Every point has an address (x, y). Distance formula = how far apart two addresses are (like Google Maps straight-line distance). Section formula = finding the address of a hotel that is 2/3 of the way from city A to city B. Area formula = how much land is enclosed by three addresses (cities). It's geography, but with algebra.
concept_section.principle: Distance: d = √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²]. Midpoint: M = ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2). Section (m:n): P = ((mx₂+nx₁)/(m+n), (my₂+ny₁)/(m+n)). Area of △ = ½|x₁(y₂−y₃) + x₂(y₃−y₁) + x₃(y₁−y₂)|.
concept_section.reveal_prompt: Tap each formula to see it applied 👇

reveals.question: 📏 Distance Formula — application?
reveals.answer: d = √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²]. Used to prove: type of triangle (equilateral if all sides equal; isoceles if 2 sides equal); points are collinear if sum of two shorter distances = longest distance; type of quadrilateral (use all 4 sides + both diagonals).

reveals.question: ✂️ Section Formula — m:n division?
reveals.answer: P divides AB in ratio m:n internally: P = ((mx₂+nx₁)/(m+n), (my₂+ny₁)/(m+n)). Midpoint is special case where m=n=1. For external division: same formula but with minus sign. If P divides AB in ratio k:1, substitute m=k, n=1 to simplify.

reveals.question: △ Area of Triangle?
reveals.answer: Area = ½|x₁(y₂−y₃) + x₂(y₃−y₁) + x₃(y₁−y₂)|. If area = 0, points are collinear! This is a useful test for collinearity. Always take absolute value to get positive area.

reveals.question: 🔵 Types of quadrilateral — coordinate proof?
reveals.answer: To prove ABCD is a: parallelogram (diagonals bisect each other → midpoints equal); rectangle (parallelogram + diagonals equal); rhombus (all sides equal + diagonals not equal); square (all sides equal + diagonals equal). Calculate all 4 sides AND both diagonals.

points: Area of triangle: ½|x₁(y₂−y₃) + x₂(y₃−y₁) + x₃(y₁−y₂)|; zero means collinear
Quadrilateral proof: always compute all 4 sides + both diagonals for complete proof

exam_questions.question: Find the coordinates of a point P that divides the line segment joining A(4,−3) and B(9,7) in the ratio 3:2 internally.
Find the area of triangle with vertices A(1,2), B(3,0), C(5,4). Hence check if the three points are collinear.
Find the distance between points P(4,−3) and Q(−2,5).

quiz.exp: d = √[(3−0)² + (4−0)²] = √[9+16] = √25 = 5. This is the classic 3-4-5 right triangle.
Midpoint = ((2+8)/2, (6+4)/2) = (10/2, 10/2) = (5,5). Average of x-coordinates and average of y-coordinates.

quiz.q: If area of triangle with given vertices is 0, the points are:
quiz.exp: Area = 0 means no enclosed space — the three points lie on the same straight line, i.e., they are collinear. This is a quick test for collinearity.

quiz.q: Point P divides A(1,2) and B(7,8) in ratio 1:2. P is:

flipcards.front: Section formula for m:n internal division?
If area of triangle = 0, what does that mean?
flipcards.back: The three points are collinear (lie on same line)

flipcards.front: To prove ABCD is a rectangle?
flipcards.back: Show: all 4 sides equal (or opposite sides equal) AND both diagonals are equal
